fields: IAM's name
territory sets
In the field's terms
CpG island and partially methylated domain (PMD) region sets
Definition

An input identifying the site groups that lie outside the identity sites: the CpG islands and the loosely held (partially methylated) domains, as defined by the atlas's territory sets, with the value given as islands 66,986; loosely held domains.
What it does
It supplies the territory sets — the islands and the loosely held domains — so that the instrument's job, 'changes outside identity sites,' can be carried out across those site groups.
Why the instrument needs it
The instrument needs a defined set of territories to know which sites count as islands versus loosely held domains before it can read entropy change outside the identity sites.
How it is obtained or computed
Each territory is read at its expected value for the sample's own read depth, against the atlas (field_how), drawing on the measured territories.sets input with basis measured (atlas).
Where it is read
At CpG islands (islands 66,986) and at partially methylated (loosely held) domains across the genome, outside the identity sites.
Where IAM's Law enters

This row is explicitly marked law_part: 'not the law itself: a measured input the law uses' and lf_section: 'not part of IAM's Law.' It is a measured territory-definition input — not a step in IAM's Law — that the law subsequently draws on.

not part of IAM's Law
Healthy value and how it is set

The value is islands 66,986; loosely held domains, drawn from territories.sets with basis measured (atlas), sourced from the IAM Sequencing Atlas (measured healthy reference); card_key notes it is not yet on the card.
Where its value comes from
the IAM Sequencing Atlas (measured healthy reference)

fields: How it works

Two territories read separately against the IAM Sequencing Atlas, each at its expected value for the sample's own read count: CpG islands (66,986 sites every healthy type keeps unmarked) and loosely held (partially methylated) domains.
Why
Many departures from healthy occur outside the identity sites: island gain and domain loss. Reading them under their own masks keeps one from hiding the other.
Physics
IAM's Law, link 1d: islands carry only the meter; domains' healthy level is IAM-A's held error at the site's loose share.
Where the data comes from
The sample's molecules; the territory sets; the atlas's sealed donor halves (terr_half_counts_v1) for held-out reading.
The numbers
Held-out pass 8: domains 0.993 +/- 0.234, islands 1.011 +/- 0.327. Healthy pass 5 (islands against the other donor half): met. Relay test: planted island gain moved island territories x9.96.
Method and standard
Counted expectation at the sample's read depth (synthetic met 2026-11-01); bars by the 2026-11-07 rule from held-out pass 9 (owed).
Known-answer test
Relay test (2026-11-20): planted island gain moved the island territory x9.96 (met).
Limits
(1) Site sets are array-sited; sequencing-sited sets owed. (2) Wide held-out widths (thin donors). (3) Domains depend on Met-A's expectation and move with the tare.
Where the result goes
bundle territories (islands, domains, state); report.
Code
stage_metaa_atlas territories; terr_half_counts_v1
How to rebuild it
1. Take the island and domain sets. 2. Expected disorder at each site's read count from the atlas (or the other donor half). 3. Sample over expected per territory.
History
Dated entries in the development log (METHYLPHYS_DEVELOPMENT_LOG.md) and the instrument's development record.
records.name: Territories: islands and loosely held domains, read outside the identity sites
questions: Why read islands and domains separately?
Departures typically gain marks at islands and lose them in loosely held domains; mixed together, one change can hide the other.
Is there currently an established healthy range for the islands and domains scores, or is the 0.95-1.05 window in the code a validated reference?

There is no healthy band yet. The center (the type's healthy median) and width (measured spread) still need to be set from the 152 atlas libraries. The 0.95-1.05 figure currently in the code is only a holdover, not an established healthy range, and this applies to both the islands and domains outputs as well as to the overall territories state.
instrument record: outputs (Territories, islands / Territories, domains / Territories state) healthy_how and limits fields
How many CpG island sites make up the islands territory reading?
66,986 sites, defined as sites that every healthy cell type keeps unmarked.
What happens to cell types that make up only a small share of a sample when computing the Territories score?
Cells below a minimum share of the sample are left out of the territories score. The minimum is a rule of the pipeline, not a measured quantity; its value is not yet printed beside the reading.
